communications.subject: Alaska Public Records Act Request: Parole Board Member Terms and Salaries (Alaska Board Of Parole)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Alaska Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

-the current term expiration date (month, day, and year) for each parole board member
-the annual salary / total compensation for each parole board member for 2026 

I am making this request for research purposes and am not a journalist.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Wourms

communications.subject: ACTION REQUIRED / Alaska DOC public records request / Parole Board
communications.communication:
In the future, to ensure efficient processing, please submit your request through the appropriate portal: https://doc.alaska.gov/public-records-request.
Do not send requests directly to the facility.

Per AS 40.25.122 and 2 AAC 96.220, the Department may ask if a requester is a party or represents a party in an administrative or judicial litigation with the state in which a requested record is relevant. If the answer is YES, the requester must seek the records in accordance with the rules of procedure applicable in the administrative or judicial proceeding.



Please "reply" to this email: Are you such a requestor? (currently in litigation with the state of Alaska)

Yes or no.


It is important to note there may be a cost associated with public records searches, an estimate of which is based on the parameters of your search. Alaska Statute 40.25.110 (c) allows "if the production of records for one requester in a calendar month exceeds five person-hours, the public agency shall require the requester to pay the personnel costs required during the month to complete the search and copying tasks." Additionally, you would need to pay the fee before the records are disclosed. If it is determined this request will exceed five person hours, I can provide you with an estimated cost of the search. Please note that the estimate is for costs associated with searching DOC records and is no guarantee that any responsive records exist. We may not locate any records responsive to your request, and you will still be charged the search fee. If responsive records are located, then those documents allowable for release will be made available to you.



For clarification, please refer to AS 40.25.115 (a) which says, "activities authorized under this section may not take priority over the primary responsibilities of the public agency." Additionally, DOC P&P 108.07 (VII) (B) states "no response shall be sent to a requestor prior to informing and consulting with the Commissioner, Division Director and Department of Law."


Respectfully,
Betsy

title: Public Information Act Request — RFCSP #22-201 Strategic Planning Facilitation: proposals, scoring, negotiation and award records

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Public Information Act Request — RFCSP #22-201 Strategic Planning Facilitation: proposals, scoring, negotiation and award records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Texas Public Information Act (Government Code Chapter 552), I request copies of the following records relating to Richardson Independent School District RFCSP #22-201, "Strategic Planning Facilitation" (released on or about November 2022; proposals due November 28, 2022; awarded to Engage!Learning Inc., also known as engage2learn). The date range for this request is November 1, 2022 through September 30, 2026.

In this request, a reference to any record includes that record under any title the District uses for it; where a title differs, I request the record that serves that function.

1. The complete solicitation document for RFCSP #22-201, including all addenda, the evaluation criteria and weights, and any document stating a budget, estimated cost, or not-to-exceed amount for this procurement.
2. The bid/proposal tabulation (also called a bid abstract, proposal register, or log of proposals received) showing all proposers and all proposed prices, in its native spreadsheet format if maintained as one.
3. All evaluation and scoring records, including: scoring sheets (also called evaluation forms, rating sheets, or scorecards), individual evaluator scores and any consensus or summary scores, scoring rubrics, evaluator comments and worksheets (also called committee notes), and any scores or evaluations from vendor presentations, demonstrations, or interviews. This includes evaluation records and exports maintained in the District's electronic bidding system (Bonfire) or any other e-procurement system.
4. All proposals submitted in response to RFCSP #22-201, including both technical proposals and cost proposals (including any cost proposals submitted under separate cover) from all proposers. If the volume is large, I prioritize: (a) the proposal of Engage!Learning Inc./engage2learn
5. Records and correspondence between the District and the selected proposer regarding price and negotiation, including any best-and-final-offer (BAFO) requests and responses, and any documents showing a revised or negotiated price.
6. The executed contract (also called the agreement or professional services agreement) with the selected proposer, including scope of work, final price, term, and renewal options, plus all amendments, change orders, and extensions.
7. The board agenda item and supporting materials approving this award, including any statement of the funding source (for example, general fund or a grant) and the budgeted amount; if a grant or foundation funded any part of this procurement, the grant agreement or memorandum of understanding; or other records sufficient to identify the funding source and the budgeted amount.
8. Line-item invoices submitted by, and payments (also called payment records or disbursement records) made to, the selected proposer under this contract, from the contract start through September 30, 2026.
9. The final deliverable(s) (also called work products or final reports) produced under this contract, including the adopted strategic plan document.

Please provide records in electronic format (native files, including spreadsheets where maintained, or searchable PDF) where available, and produce records on a rolling basis as they are located and reviewed, beginning with the tabulation, scoring records, and executed contract, rather than holding all records until the full set is complete. If a responsive record is held by a third-party portal or vendor on the District's behalf, please produce it or identify where it is publicly posted. If any portion of a record is withheld or redacted, please cite the specific statutory exception relied upon and release all reasonably segregable portions. If fees are expected to exceed $50, please contact me with an itemized estimate before processing so I may narrow the request; I do not authorize fees above $50 without my prior written approval.

Thank you.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Felipe Acano

title: Third-Party-Owned Flock Hardware (Savannah City Clerk)

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Third-Party-Owned Flock Hardware (Savannah City Clerk)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any contract, master services agreement, memorandum of understanding or agreement, interlocal or intergovernmental agreement, grant agreement, nondisclosure agreement, or similar document between the Savannah Police Department and any of the following that concerns Flock Safety cameras, solar panels, mounting or power equipment, or other Flock hardware: (a) the Savannah Area Regional Intelligence Center (SARIC); (b) the Georgia Information Sharing and Analysis Center (GISAC); (c) any High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) program; (d) the Georgia Bureau of Investigation or any other regional intelligence center, fusion center, or task force; or (e) any agency, institution, or private party other than the City of Savannah and Flock Safety.
Existing records, such as asset inventories, purchase orders, invoices, grant award documents, installation or deployment records, or hardware lists from the Department's Flock account, sufficient to identify any Flock camera, solar panel, or other Flock hardware used by the Department that is owned, funded, leased, or installed by an entity other than the City of Savannah, including that entity's name.

This request includes responsive records that Flock Safety or another private contractor maintains on the City's behalf. See O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a)(2)(B). If any responsive record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as § 50-18-71(d) provides, and produce all reasonably segregable portions.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

title: Deaths-in-custody

communications.subject: Ohio Open Records Law Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Ohio Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Barnstable Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Barnstable Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff

___________________________________________________________________
Also note that after a thorough review of our files, the Salem Police Department's Records Office has identified an email responsive to your request. However, we are unable to release this record, as it is legally exempt from mandatory public disclosure.
Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law<https://www.mass.gov/files/2017-06/Public%20Records%20Law.pdf>, G.L. c. 4, § 7(26)<https://www.mass.gov/info-details/exemptions>, the requested email is being withheld in its entirety under the following legal protections:
Basis for Exemption

  *
Common Law Attorney-Client Privilege: Under established Massachusetts common law, confidential communications between a governmental entity and its legal counsel are strictly protected from disclosure to ensure the public entity can obtain candid, reliable legal advice. See Suffolk Construction Co. v. Division of Capital Asset Management, 449 Mass. 444 (2007). The withheld email (dated 8-24-26) is that of the Chief of Police Lucas Miller. It is a confidential communication sent to Eric Atstupenas, the General Counsel for the Massachusetts Chiefs of Police Association seeking specific legal advisement on policy and protocol interpretations regarding Protect Act compliance.
  *
Exemption (d) — Deliberative Process / Policy Development: Pursuant to G.L. c. 4, § 7(26)(d)<https://www.mass.gov/guide-to-evidence/section-518-executive-or-governmental-privilege>, public records do not include intra-agency or inter-agency memos or letters relating to policy positions currently being developed. This email consists of pre-decisional protocol and policy questions aimed at establishing compliance frameworks. Release of this preliminary, deliberative information would stifle the free, honest exchange of ideas required for law enforcement agencies to successfully navigate new regulatory requirements.

Due to the fact that the entire substance of the communication consists of a request for legal consultation and ongoing policy formulation, there are no segregable, purely factual portions that can be redacted and released.
No additional responsive records were located in the custody or control of this office.

Please be advised that pursuant to 950 CMR 32.00 and G.L. c. 66, § 10A(a), you have the right to appeal this decision to the Supervisor of Public Records within 90 calendar days. Such appeal must be in writing and should include a copy of your original request and, if available, this response. Please note that the Supervisor may only consider appeals arising from written public records requests. Pursuant to G.L. c. 66, § 10A(c), you also have the right to seek judicial review by commencing a civil action in Superior Court.

communications.subject: Re: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Brookline Police Department)
communications.communication:
Hi,
I am responding to your request below:
 Pursuant to your October 23, 2026 public records request copied below, in regards to Portions #1 and #2 of your request, in an effort of transparency policies and procedures for the Brookline Police Department are available to the public at all times; no PRRs are needed to view any of these materials. Please see the following link for full list of Department policies and procedures:
https://www.brooklinepolice.com/185/Brookline-Police-Policies-and-Procedures<https://protect-us.mimecast.com/s/K-XBCOY58ku06L7wiESm_X?domain=brooklinepolice.com>
In regards to portion #3 in the attached PRR; The mandatory disclosure provision of the Public Records Law only applies to information that is in the custody of the Department at the time the request is received. As a result, there is no obligation for a department to create a record for a requester to honor a request. See G.L. c. 4, section 7(26) (defining "public records" as materials which have already been "made or received" by a public entity); see also 32 Op. Attorney Gen. 157, 165 (May 18, 1977) (custodian is not obliged to create a record in response to a request for information); see also A Guide to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Division of Public Records, p. 7 (January 2013) (hereinafter Public Records Guide). As such the Department has no materials to release.
 There are no fees associated with this request.  At this time the Department considers this request closed.
 You have the right to appeal this determination to the supervisor of records pursuant to G.L. c.66, § 10A(a) and the right to seek judicial review of an unfavorable decision by commencing a civil action in superior court under G.L. c.66, §10A(c).  Any and all appeals should be filed through the Sec of the Commonwealth.
 Signed,
Amanda Williams
Records Clerk
Brookline Police Department

communications.subject: Oregon Public Records Law Request: Multnomah County Medical Examiner's Office: Public records request: disposition records, unidentified female decedent, Portland, October 18, 1994
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of the following records concerning an unidentified adult female found deceased in a Portland hotel room on October 18, 1994. This unidentified adult female is listed as NamUs #UP9936, has a Portland Police Bureau agency case number of 94-99422, and has an Oregon State Police Medical Examiner's Office agency case number of 94-2962. The decedent is unidentified and was recorded under an
alias at hotel check-in.

The NAMUS listing can be found online at:
https://www.namus.gov/UnidentifiedPersons/Case#/9936/contacts?nav

There is a Websleuth's thread located online at:
https://websleuths.com/threads/or-portland-whtfem-35-55-up9936-suicide-hotel-surgical-scars-lft-knee-rt-breast-dec94.165575/

Under the Oregon Public Records Law (ORS 192.311 et seq.), I request copies of the following records concerning an unidentified adult female found deceased in a Portland hotel room on October 18, 1994:

1. Any order for disposition of the body (burial, cremation, or reduction) issued by a medical examiner or sheriff, and any burial, cremation, or reduction permit.

2. The verified statement of expenses and any related report of death filed with the Board of County Commissioners (ORS 146.121).

3. Records identifying the funeral home, contractor, or cemetery used, and the date and location of disposition, including any plot, grave, niche, or common-grave record.

4. Any invoice, payment record, or contract for the disposition.

5. Any record of biological samples, tissue, hair, bone, slides, or dental records retained from the autopsy, and their current location.

6. If any responsive record has been destroyed, the applicable retention schedule and any destruction certificate.

I ask that fees be waived or reduced because this is in the public interest. I am an independent researcher and I have a theory as to the identity of this unidentified person. 

Thank you for the work that the Multnomah County Medical Examiner's Office does each and every day.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

communications.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] Colorado Open Records Act Request: DPD Search logs/audit logs from Axon ALPR System (Denver Police Department)
communications.communication:
Good afternoon Mr. Beckett –
Following a good faith search, please see the attached records responsive to your request available to the public. Records of the Denver Police Department are criminal justice records, the disclosure of which is governed by the Colorado Criminal Justice Records Act (CCJRA), sections 24-72-301, et. seq. C.R.S.  Except for records of “official actions,” the disclosure of criminal justice records is discretionary and can be denied where the custodian believes disclosure would be contrary to the public interest. Section 24-72-305(5), C.R.S.
 Pursuant to Harris v. Denver Post, 123 P.3d 116 (Colo. 2005), the following factors , in addition to other relevant considerations,  may be used to determine whether a record should be released or withheld:

  1.  the privacy interests of individuals, if any, who may be impacted by a decision to allow disclosure of the record;
  2.  the agency’s interest in keeping confidential information confidential;
  3.  the agency’s interest in the integrity of on-going investigations;
  4.  the public purpose to be served in allowing disclosure of the record; and
  5.  any other pertinent considerations relevant to the circumstances of the records request, including whether disclosure would be contrary to the public interest.
Based upon my consideration of the relevant factors, I have determined that certain information should be redacted from the report prior to public disclosure to protect privacy and interests which outweigh the public interest in disclosure of the information.  The redacted columns include, names of officers, case numbers, time frame, license plate information, search coordinates, vehicle description, filters (which included case numbers and other information related to criminal investigation)s) and entries from within the reason column have been redacted.
We also want to proactively share some important context with you regarding two entries in the May audit log.

The two queries on May 19, 2026, with the offense category listed as “Other; Immigration Violator” were test queries submitted by Denver Police personnel during DPD’s testing phase conducted prior to the go-live date of June 3, 2026, for its Axon ALPR pilot program. More specifically, the queries were submitted to see if the system would allow such a query and how it would be reported in the audit so that DPD could provide feedback to the vendor. So, to be clear, these two queries were submitted for the purpose of testing the system prior to implementation and were not submitted for the purpose of any enforcement.
In accordance with Denver municipal ordinance and Colorado law, the Denver Police Department does not assist with the enforcement of civil federal immigration laws.

Thank you,

Andrea

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Shrewsbury Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Shrewsbury Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.subject: Maryland Public Information Act Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Amherst Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Amherst Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

title: Minneapolis and St. Paul Police - LexisNexis / AVCC Data Sharing (Minneapolis Police Department)

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Minneapolis and St. Paul Police - LexisNexis / AVCC Data Sharing (Minneapolis Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

REQUEST: Please provide all emails between employees of your police department and LexisNexis from October 1, 2025 through July 28, 2026. You may de-duplicate emails if the same email was sent to multiple employees. Please include attachments. Please ensure the responsive emails and documents are preserved during the time it takes to process this request. The LexisNexis email domains are @LexisNexisRisk.com and @LexisNexis.com 

CONTEXT: During Operation Metro Surge, LexisNexis wrote an email stating that they hope to soon have data from Minneapolis Police and St. Paul Police available to subscribers of Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC). LexisNexis has AVCC contracts with, and sells data access to ICE, the Navy, the VA, the DOJ, and 2,400 federal and local agencies around the U.S., meaning they can view victim and witness details of police reports and 911 calls from departments that allow LexisNexis to copy their data. We are trying to understand whether your agency has started sharing your CAD/RMS data with federal agencies via LexisNexis's AVCC / Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: BPD Basic Data Request 11/2020
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

11/1/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of the following fields of information for all Boston Police Department employees from 11/1/2020 to 12/1/2020. Please include the following fields of information:
 
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (475)-243-3786 and mchristi@bu.edu

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

Sincerely,
Michael Christie
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

11/1/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of the following fields of information for all Boston Police Department employees from 3/1/2021 to 4/1/2021. Please include the following fields of information:
 
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2021) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (475)-243-3786 and mchristi@bu.edu

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

Sincerely,
Michael Christie
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2021) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (475)-243-3786 and mchristi@bu.edu

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

Sincerely,
Michael Christie

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

communications.subject: Florida Sunshine Law Request: flock clone (City Of Oviedo)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Florida Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

Under Article I, section 24 of the Florida Constitution and Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, I request copies of public records concerning the investigation and arrest involving an alleged decoy or replica Flock Safety camera reported by ClickOrlando on August 23, 2026.
News report: https://www.clickorlando.com/news/local/2026/08/23/oviedo-arrest-over-decoy-flock-camera-raises-questions-about-surveillance/

Please provide the following records:
- All incident, offense, arrest, supplemental, investigative, and probable-cause reports concerning the decoy or replica camera and the related arrest.

- All arrest warrants, search warrants, warrant applications, affidavits, returns, inventories, subpoenas, court orders, consent-to-search forms, and preservation requests associated with the investigation.

- All photographs, videos, body-worn-camera recordings, dashboard-camera recordings, surveillance footage, drone footage, diagrams, measurements, maps, sketches, and scene documentation depicting the device, its installation, its location, or its removal.

- All records concerning the design, creation, fabrication, assembly, installation, operation, intended use, or testing of the alleged decoy camera that were obtained, collected, copied, downloaded, submitted, or created during the investigation.

This specifically includes, without limitation:
Native 3D-printing and design files, including STL, 3MF, OBJ, AMF, STEP, STP, IGES, CAD, OpenSCAD, Blender, Fusion 360, SolidWorks, Cura, PrusaSlicer, G-code, project, and slicer-profile files;

Drawings, schematics, dimensions, measurements, templates, parts lists, bills of materials, assembly instructions, build notes, revisions, prototypes, and design histories;

Source images, photographs, scans, photogrammetry files, reference models, and specifications used to reproduce the appearance of a Flock Safety camera;

Files or instructions obtained from websites, cloud services, social-media accounts, messaging platforms, removable media, computers, phones, or other digital devices; and

Any investigative copies, forensic images, exports, screenshots, printouts, or derivative versions of these materials.

All communications concerning this incident between or among the Oviedo Police Department and:

Flock Safety or its representatives;

The City of Oviedo;

The Seminole County Sheriff’s Office;

The State Attorney’s Office;

Other law-enforcement agencies;

Property owners, homeowners’ associations, utilities, or contractors; and

Members of the public, witnesses, complainants, or news organizations.

This includes emails, attachments, text messages, messaging-app communications, memoranda, letters, call logs, meeting notes, and communications sent through personal accounts or devices when used for official business.

Any press releases, media talking points, public statements, internal summaries, briefing materials, or records prepared in response to media inquiries regarding this incident.

Requested format

Please provide records electronically by email or downloadable link. For electronic records—particularly design, CAD, 3D-printing, source-code, configuration, and metadata-bearing files—I request the native electronic files in the format in which the agency maintains or received them. Please do not substitute screenshots, paper printouts, or flattened PDF versions when native files exist.

Please preserve associated metadata, original filenames, directory structure, and available creation and modification dates. If forensic software does not permit production in native form, please provide the ordinary export format and any accompanying report that identifies the original filename, path, metadata, and hash value.

Please do not withhold an entire record merely because one portion is exempt. If records are held by another department, employee, contractor, cloud provider, forensic vendor, or agency on the City’s behalf, please include those records or identify the appropriate custodian.

Please acknowledge receipt and provide an estimated production date. If responsive records can be produced on a rolling basis, please provide them as they become available rather than waiting until the entire request is complete.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Jason Koebler

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Safety Event Log, May 15, 2026 to Present
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting the Flock Safety Event Log for the Savannah Police Department’s Flock account, covering every organization or network in the account, from May 15, 2026, through the date of this request. This is the export of user and administrative actions with the columns Timestamp, User, Event Type, Entity Type, Entity Details, and Event Id. It is not the license plate search audit.

In priority order:

Every event other than live stream views, for example, network share changes (create, update, or delete), custom hotlist entries, recorded stream views, and stream downloads.
The live stream view events.
Any documentation from Flock or kept by the Department that explains the Event Log’s fields, event types, and entity types.

If item 2 is large or costly, please send items 1 and 3 first and give me the estimate for item 2. I am glad to narrow its date range or scope.

Please provide the log as a CSV or the platform’s native export so I can search it. If the platform limits the export size or period, please provide as many exports as needed to cover the whole period with no gaps, and tell me the first and last event date in each file. This includes records Flock Safety maintains for the Department. See O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a)(2)(B).

If any part cannot be released, please tell me which part and the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as § 50-18-71(d) provides, and release the rest. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

communications.subject: RE: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Safety Event Log, May 15, 2026 to Present
communications.communication:
Thank you for the two worksheets. Three things are still missing.

First, user names. The request asked for a User column, but the file gives only a User External ID code. Please provide the Flock user list mapping each External ID to the user’s name, role, and account status, or add the names.

Second, the entity column. Section 35-1-22(f) exempts captured license plate data, which section 35-1-22(a)(2) defines as the coordinates, date and time, photograph, and plate number captured by or derived from the license plate system. Camera and stream names, the organizations a network was shared with, role names, and user-account names are not that data. Please restore the entity column for every row except the Custom Hotlist Entry rows, and for the hotlist rows, blank the plate number and release the rest. That is a column edit and does not need review of individual cells, so I am not asking for the cell-by-cell review described in your message.

Third, if the Department still withholds entity information under § 50-18-72(a)(4), please identify the paragraph and the pending investigation it relates to, as § 50-18-71(d) provides, and release the rest.

Item 3 of my request (documentation explaining the Event Log’s fields, event types, and entity types) was not addressed. Please provide it or tell me in writing that none exists. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

Written requests for records to state and local agencies in Pennsylvania are generally governed by the Commonwealth’s Right-to-Know Law (RTKL), 65 P.S. §§ 67.101-67.3104. In accordance with the RTKL, the City has promulgated an Open Records Policy, which requires the standard statewide Right-to-Know Form be used for the submission of written requests pursuant to the RTKL. Gaming Control Bd. v. Office of Open Records, 48 A.3d 503 (Pa. Cmmw. 2012). The City reserves the right to require a formal RTK Request be submitted pursuant to the RTKL before releasing records. Please include this notice with your RTK Request. The City reserves the right to assert any and all grounds of denial in its final response to your request.  Respectfully,  Margot B. Smith    Chief Deputy City Solicitor    Right to Know Unit  City of Philadelphia Law Department    Tracking #: 53129865 41130 Request Summary: Pursuant to the Pennsylvania Right to Know Act, I hereby request the following records:  I request records of any counts of pedestrians at specific locations in the city from 2019 through 2025, showing where, on what date or dates and at what times each count was taken, and how many pedestrians were counted.  1. Pedestrian counts. All counts of pedestrians at specific locations in the city taken by or for the agency from January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2025. This includes, for example:  manual or video-based counts of people walking on sidewalks or crossing at intersections, including turning-movement counts that record crosswalk volumes;  automated pedestrian counters (for example, infrared or camera-based sensors), short-term or permanent;  counts made for specific projects, studies, before-and-after evaluations or count programs;  pedestrian counts that the agency received from other public agencies, business improvement districts or consultants.  2. What each record should show. For each count, records sufficient to show:  the location: coordinates, or the street and cross streets or block, and a site or station identifier if one is used;  the date of the count (day, month and year); for counts that ran over several days or continuously (for example, multi-day or permanent counters), the first and last date and the date of each interval;  the start and end time of each counting interval;  the number of pedestrians in each interval, at the finest time interval recorded (for example, each 15 minutes or each hour);  the count method (manual, video, or automated sensor type);  whether pedestrians are counted separately from people on bicycles or scooters;  whether the values are raw counts or adjusted or estimated figures (for example, factored to an annual average);  any flags for missing, partial or faulty intervals.  If this information exists only in raw count files, field sheets, sensor exports or reports delivered by a count contractor, I request copies of those files.  3. Documentation. For each file provided, any data dictionary, codebook, field definitions, methodology notes or other documentation that explains its columns, codes and units. communications.communication:
October 21, 2021 RE:  USAID FOIA No. F-00026-22 (FOIA Specialist Assignment Email) Dear Mr. Freudenthal: This acknowledges receipt of your October 21, 2021, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).  Specifically, you requested records concerning: All the drafts or final reports of audits and/or investigations and/or desk reviews undertaken by the Office of the Inspector General on the response to the 10th, 11th and/or 12th Ebola epidemics in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 to today. This includes any updates regarding complaint 19-0852 and 20-0502 inter alia.- All reports of the visit by a delegation of U.S. officials to the Democratic Republic of Congo to assess the response to the outbreak. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 until today-(Date Range for Record Search: From 4/14/2020 To 10/21/2021). 
Fee 
The FOIA provides that fees should be waived or reduced if disclosure of the information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.  As a member of the media, the only applicable fee is duplication.  Duplication is $0.10 per page, but the first 100 pages are free. Since the only applicable fee is duplication, and USAID routinely furnishes responsive records to FOIA requesters in electronic format, it's most likely there will be no duplication fees to assess. 
FOIA Specialist 
Your request has been assigned to Theresa Morris, Senior FOIA Specialist.  You may contact Theresa Morris by email at thmorris@usaid.gov or by phone on 202-921-5003.  Please reference the tracking number cited above in any future correspondence. 
Extending the FOIA’s Time Limits due to Unusual Circumstances The FOIA provides that an agency  may extend its time limits when “unusual circumstances” occur in the processing of a request. See 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B)(i) (2016).  Those “unusual circumstances” are set forth in the statute, 5 U.S.C § 552(a)(6)(B)(iii), and are described as: 1) The need to search for records from field facilities or other locations separate from the office processing the request; 2) The need to search, collect and examine voluminous records; and 3) The need for consultation with another agency. Based upon the records you have requested, we have determined that one or more unusual circumstances will occur during the processing of your request.  Accordingly, your response time-limit has been extended beyond the 20 days required by statute; therefore, 10 additional processing days have been added to your request. To mitigate this action, you may limit the scope of the request so that it can be processed more quickly or to arrange an alternative time to respond. If you have any questions or wish to discuss reformulation or an alternative time frame for the processing of your request, you may contact the assigned FOIA Specialist noted above. You may also contact USAID’s FOIA Public Liaison, Christopher Colbow, at foia@usaid.gov. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) 

Additionally, you may contact the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) at the National Archives and Records Administration to inquire about the FOIA mediation services offered: Office of Government Information Services National Archives and Records Administration 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001 E-mail: ogis@nara.gov Telephone: 202-741-5770; Toll Free: 1-877-684-6448 Fax: 202-741-5769 Thank you for your interest in USAID. Sincerely, Diamond Johnson

Bureau for Management 
Office of Management Services 
Information and Records Division

communications.subject: USAID FOIA Email Receipt RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #F-00026-22
communications.communication:
Greetings - 

Thank you for contacting the USAID FOIA office. We have received your request and will respond within 48 hours. 

Kindly be informed of the following: 

Requesting records containing personally identifiable information (PII): 
1st Party Request: 
If you are requesting records about yourself, we must verify your identity prior to initiating a search for records. Please complete and return t he AID form 507-1, Certification of Identity, located here: https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1. Please submit the completed form in addition to the source documents outlined in section 2 encrypted via (https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1) foia@usaid.gov, accompanied by a password in a separate email. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) 
3rd Party Request: 
If you are requesting records concerning another individual on their behalf, you must provide a statement from that individual verifying their identity. Please have the subject of the request complete sections 1 and 2 of the AID form 507-1, Certification of Identity, located here: https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1. As the 3rd party requester, please complete section 3. Send the completed form and source documents outlined in section 2 encrypted via (https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1) foia@usaid.gov, accompanied by a password, prior initiating a search for records. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) 
Requesting acquisition (contracts, etc.) and assistance (grants, cooperative agreements, etc.) awards: 

We receive many requests for procurement documents: solicitations, proposals, and contracts. Sometimes our requesters only provide us with the solicitation number. If possible, when you are requesting winning proposals, please provide the following additional information: the office that issued the solicitation, the title of the solicitation, the name of the successful bidder, and the number of the resulting award. For procurement documents, please provide the award number, office that issued the award, program name, and geographic location. 

Thank you, 

USAID FOIA Team 

-- 
V/r, FOIA Specialist US AID - US Agency for International Development FOIA Office Bureau for Management, Office of Management Services, Information and Records Division (M/MS/IRD) | foia@USAID.gov

communications.subject: Oregon Public Records Law Request: EMAILS REGARDING BEND POLICE
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Specifically, I am requesting the following emails generated or received between January 1, 2024, and the date this request is processed: Copies of all formal and informal comments or complaints,  filed by members of the public or city employees regarding the conduct, policies, or actions of the City of Bend Police Department.  Copies of the 96 emails categorized under the "Police" topic sent to the City Council across the 2024, 2025, and 2026 calendar years dashboard.   

I request a full waiver of all fees associated with fulfilling this request. As a representative of the independent news outlet StateCreated.net, I am requesting this information for news-gathering and publication purposes. The disclosure of these records is in the public interest because it will significantly contribute to public understanding of local law enforcement operations, accountability mechanisms, and community relations.If this request is denied in whole or in part, please justify all deletions or redactions by reference to specific exemptions in the public records law. If portions of these records are exempt, please redact the exempt portions and release the remainder of the records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Tristann Harrison

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: Fatal Crash Involving East Fishkill Police Officer - December 2023
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

All records related to the fatal single-vehicle crash involving an East Fishkill Police Department officer on or around December 18, 2023, including but not limited to:

1. Crash/accident reports (MV-104 or equivalent)
2. Collision Reconstruction Unit reports
3. Body-worn camera footage from responding troopers
4. Photographs of the scene and vehicle
5. Toxicology/blood alcohol results for the officer involved
6. Any internal investigation or review documents
7. Communications (radio logs, CAD records) related to the incident

This incident was previously assigned FOIL Number NYSP-23-12-1655. That request was denied and appealed in January 2024

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

EJ Fox

Due to the government furlough that occurred from 1 October 2025 to 12 November 2025, the Department of the Navy was legally required to suspend all non-excepted operations, including the processing of Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests. communications.subject: Request Received 2026-NavyFOIA-006381
communications.communication:
Good Day, 

Your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request of March 1, 2026 has been received by the Navy Personnel Command (NPC).  This command received your request on April 1, 2026. Your FOIA request number is 2026-NavyFOIA-006382 and your FOIA correspondence file number is 6NPC0485. 

Due to the government furlough that occurred from 1 October 2025 to 12 November 2025, the Department of the Navy was legally required to suspend all non-excepted operations, including the processing of Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests. During this period, FOIA personnel were prohibited from performing their duties, which resulted in unavoidable delays and a temporary halt in responding to pending inquiries. In addition, FOIA analysts who were furloughed lost access to the online Navy FOIA tracking system, Secure Release, until 10 December 2025. Now that normal operations have resumed, the FOIA Office is working diligently to address the backlog created by the furlough, and the holidays and is committed to processing requests as efficiently and transparently as possible. We appreciate the your patience and understanding during this interruption in service. 

The records you seek require a search in and/or consultation with another office, and so your request falls within the "unusual circumstances" See 5 U.S.C. § 552 (a)(6)(B)(i)-(iii).  Because of these unusual circumstances, we may need to extend the time limit to respond to your request beyond the twenty days provided by the statute.  For your information, we use multiple tracks to process requests, but within the tracks we working an agile manner.  The time needed to complete our work on your request will necessarily depend on a variety of factors, including the complexity of a records search, the volume and complexity of any material located, and the order of receipt of your request.  At this time we have assigned your request to the complex track.  Any decision with regard to the application of fees will be made only after we determine whether fees will be implicated for this request.

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Attleboro Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)
